text: In Hungary and its history, Hungarian society, government, and individuals prioritize the preservation of Hungarian identity and culture, encompassing language, religion, and ethnicity, through both policies and personal actions. This concerted effort aims to maintain and reinforce the distinctiveness of Hungarian identity and culture. Immigrants, other cultures, and Hungarian products are expected to adapt to the Hungarian way of life or may receive protection. The importance and uniqueness of Hungarian identity are widely acknowledged, with a historical emphasis on preserving linguistic and ethnic diversity. This behavior is regarded as a significant aspect of Hungarian society by a considerable portion of the sampled population, reflecting the value placed on cultural preservation and integration within Hungarian society.

In Hungary and Hungarian society, the government and citizens engage in providing and utilizing universal healthcare, experiencing culture shock, and adapting to system changes. The goal is to ensure healthcare accessibility, survive, and adapt to the evolving system. Hungarian citizens and NGOs reciprocate by utilizing healthcare services and addressing migration issues. This behavior is influenced by a high tax rate, the preservation of cultural heritage, and financial support through VAT reduction. While not universally embraced, a significant portion of the sampled population considers this behavior as somewhat normative within Hungarian society.

In the music scene of Hungary, both musicians and listeners actively engage in creating, performing, and enjoying a diverse range of music, encompassing folk, rock, and pop genres. This behavior serves the dual purpose of expressing personal perspectives and preserving the rich cultural heritage, while also providing entertainment. Musicians often incorporate Hungarian and English lyrics, drawing inspiration from international artists and blending traditional folk elements with modern influences. This musical expression is widely regarded as a common and standard practice within the sampled population, reflecting the significant role of music in Hungarian society. The normativity of this behavior indicates that a substantial portion of the sampled population considers it a typical and accepted part of Hungarian cultural identity.

In Hungary and abroad, Hungarian people and their products express a strong sense of national pride by showcasing and celebrating Hungarian culture, language, and products. This pride is coupled with an openness to adapt to and understand different cultures, reflecting a goal of cultural exchange and mutual understanding. Simultaneously, other nations and people engage with non-Hungarian products and interact with foreigners, indicating a reciprocal cultural exchange. The Hungarian language, known for its uniqueness and complexity, is intertwined with a history of political and military influence on the culture and language. This behavior is widely regarded as normative within the sampled population, reflecting a prevalent embrace of national pride and cultural exchange.

In Hungarian online communities and literature, Hungarian authors and readers actively participate in reading, writing, and recommending literature, often in the original language. Their goal is to express emotions, influence society, and derive enjoyment from literature. This behavior forms a strong creator-reader relationship, with Hungarian society and readers engaging in reading and considering recommendations. Hungarian literature, which often includes historical adventure and depressive themes, is also frequently translated. This cultural practice of engaging with literature in its original language and the active involvement of creators and readers is widely regarded as a normative behavior within Hungarian society, with a significant portion of the sampled population actively participating in and valuing this literary exchange.

In the Hungarian film industry, Hungarian filmmakers, actors, and the government actively engage in producing, creating, and supporting films with the goal of entertaining, expressing cultural identity, and providing financial support. This includes the commendable practice of employing disabled actors, showcasing a commitment to inclusivity and diversity. The Hungarian audience, in turn, participates by watching, enjoying, and engaging with these films. The films themselves vary widely, ranging from minimal dramas to poetry-based productions, with some facing cancellation while others are of high quality. This inclusive approach to filmmaking, including the employment of disabled actors, is regarded as a significant and accepted practice within the sampled population, reflecting a normative behavior within the Hungarian film industry.

In Hungary and Hungarian cuisine, Hungarian people are known to consume and offer a diverse array of dishes, including goulash soup, pasta-like dishes, vegetable stews, soups, traditional peasant meals, and cakes. This behavior serves the dual purpose of satisfying hunger and cravings, as well as presenting food to themselves and others. The food is often perceived as traditional and robust, with certain dishes being officially protected. This culinary tradition is considered a significant aspect of Hungarian culture and is widely regarded as a normative practice by a considerable portion of the sampled population.

In Hungary, interactions between Hungarian people and foreigners vary from familiar to distant, and it is common for Hungarian individuals to appreciate foreigners' efforts to speak Hungarian, using the language in daily life. They may also express frustration when foreigners do not speak Hungarian. The goal of this behavior is to facilitate communication and express respect. In response, foreigners may speak Hungarian or foreign languages and express confusion or frustration. Hungarian is widely regarded as a difficult language, which may contribute to the appreciation for foreigners attempting to speak it. Additionally, Hungarian people are known for their hospitality and customer-centricity. This behavior is considered normative by a significant portion of the sampled population, reflecting the value placed on language and communication in Hungarian culture.

In the Hungarian political sphere, various actors such as politicians, political parties, and citizens actively express their opinions, criticisms, and engage in political activities to influence outcomes. This behavior is met with responses from political opponents and society at large, leading to ongoing political discourse and opposition based on differing political affiliations. However, this political landscape is also characterized by a perception of corruption, nepotism, and clowning within the political arena. The sampled population views this behavior as somewhat controversial and not universally accepted, with a significant portion expressing skepticism or disapproval.

In Hungarian society and schools, the Hungarian government and educational institutions actively promote anti-LGBTQ attitudes and policies, perpetuating oppressive laws that associate LGBTQ individuals with pedophilia and endorse conversion therapy. This behavior aims to suppress and discriminate against the LGBTQ+ community, subjecting them to societal pressure and oppression. Despite some innovative job opportunities in the high-tech market and advancements towards equality for gay marriage, the promotion of anti-LGBTQ attitudes and policies is highly controversial among the sampled population. This behavior is considered an unusual and divisive stance within Hungarian society, with a significant portion of the sampled population expressing disapproval of these actions.

In the Hungarian job market and workplace, Hungarian workers and unions actively advocate for fair wages, job opportunities, and labor rights with the goal of achieving better working conditions and fair compensation. This behavior is met with reciprocal actions from employers and society, who provide job opportunities and engage in negotiations with unions. However, the job market in Hungary presents challenges such as job availability, flexible work hours, and the concept of unlimited home office. The sampled population is divided in their perception of this behavior, with around half considering it normative and the other half expressing differing views. This indicates that the pursuit of fair labor practices and compensation is a topic of significant debate and varying perspectives within Hungarian society.

In Hungarian naming conventions and language use, both Hungarians and foreigners adhere to a unique naming order with the family name placed first, adapt non-Hungarian names to Hungarian phonetics, and maintain a distinct language. The goal of this behavior is to avoid confusion and facilitate pronunciation for both Hungarian and non-Hungarian names. Recipients, whether they have Hungarian or non-Hungarian names, are expected to accept and adapt to this unique naming order and pronunciation. Hungarian names often reference a place and are in a "reversed order" compared to Western names. This behavior is widely regarded as the standard and normative within the sampled population, reflecting the importance placed on maintaining the distinctiveness of Hungarian naming conventions and language use.

In the context of education and language learning within the Hungarian cultural group, both teachers and students engage in the teaching and learning of the Hungarian language and literature. This includes delving into complex language structures and cultural references, with a particular emphasis on agglutinative grammar and uráli logic. The goal of this behavior is to enhance language skills and gain a deeper understanding of cultural references. Students and foreigners reciprocate by actively learning and adapting to the intricacies of the language and culture. It is common for students to be grouped based on language proficiency, leading to frequent debates about correct language usage and comparisons of Hungarian language difficulty with other languages. This approach to language learning is widely regarded as the standard within the sampled population.

Within the Hungarian education system, the government, universities, and schools collectively aim to provide a diverse array of educational opportunities, encompassing religious and state-run schools, business education, and literature education. This approach is designed to promote diversity, multiculturalism, and standardization, while also offering financial support and striving to eliminate disparities. Students, as the recipients, benefit from this system by receiving education and financial assistance. It is noteworthy that credentialism is present within the Hungarian school system. This multifaceted approach to education is perceived as relatively common among a significant portion of the sampled population, reflecting a moderate level of normativity within the cultural context.

In the context of driving and transportation in Hungary, both drivers and authorities are observed to adhere to a driving style that aligns with the flow of traffic, utilizing public transportation, and designating specific areas for drivers. The goal of this behavior is to ensure safe and efficient driving, as well as to maintain a sense of enjoyment and control while on the road. Additionally, car ownership holds a significant status within Hungarian culture, influencing driving behaviors. The observed normativity of this driving culture is relatively high within the sampled population, indicating that a significant portion of the population agrees with and practices these driving behaviors. This driving culture is also influenced by the country's road infrastructure and traffic conditions.

In Hungarian social interactions, it is customary for Hungarian individuals to engage in various greeting practices, such as handshakes, kisses on the cheek, and verbal greetings, depending on the time of day and the desire to avoid confrontation. These practices aim to demonstrate respect, politeness, and the maintenance of personal space within acquaintances and social interactions. Foreign individuals and people they encounter during the day are expected to respond to these greetings accordingly. However, it is important to note that these greeting norms are gradually becoming less common due to the impact of the virus. Despite this, a significant portion of the sampled population still regards these traditional greeting practices as normative within Hungarian social interactions.

In Hungary, particularly in villages and suburbs, people and neighbors engage in small talk and treat each other with varying degrees of friendliness, depending on the size of the town or settlement. This behavior aims to socialize and maintain social harmony, with discussions often revolving around topics such as costs and earnings. Neighbors, acquaintances, and strangers participate in small talk and avoid certain sensitive topics to uphold a sense of community. The normativity of this behavior is perceived as moderate, with around half of the sampled population agreeing that this social interaction pattern is common within Hungarian villages and suburbs.

In the context of Hungarian language and communication, Hungarian speakers exhibit specific language conventions such as vowel harmony, informal language usage, and pronunciation adjustments. These behaviors aim to facilitate effective communication, maintain respect, and adapt to the living language, with recipients typically engaging in active listening and learning. The Hungarian language, being almost entirely phonetic with remnants of the Old Hungarian language, influences these communication norms. This set of language conventions is widely regarded as a standard practice within the Hungarian cultural group, with a significant portion of the sampled population acknowledging and adhering to these linguistic customs.

In the Hungarian political system, both Hungarian citizens and the government actively engage in the democratic process through voting, expressing support, and opposition, with the goal of influencing governance. Simultaneously, the government and political parties conduct elections and govern the country. This reciprocal relationship between the citizens and the government reflects a commitment to political participation and the preservation of normalcy within the system. Additionally, there is an emphasis on the dissolution of the National Electoral Roll (NER) as part of this engagement. This behavior is regarded as a common practice among a significant portion of the sampled population, indicating a normative approach to citizen-government interaction and political participation within the Hungarian cultural context.

When it comes to watching movies and TV shows, Hungarians have a preference for experiencing content in its original language with subtitles, aiming to enhance their enjoyment and understanding. Additionally, they particularly enjoy reality shows and have a tendency to favor Hungarian-dubbed content. This preference for original language with subtitles and Hungarian-dubbed content is influenced by the limited availability of TV channels in the past. While this behavior is not unanimously prevalent among the sampled population, it is considered a moderately common practice within Hungarian culture.

In Hungary and other Central European and Balkan countries, Hungarian people are known to produce and consume Pálinka, a traditional fruit brandy, with an annual production of up to 82 liters per person. The goal behind this behavior is to enjoy and share this traditional drink, which is made from Hungarian fruits and comes in varying tastes from bitter to sweet. Pálinka holds significant cultural importance in Hungary and is often shared with foreign friends and consumers, who are expected to consume and appreciate this traditional beverage. This practice is widely regarded as a normative and integral part of Hungarian culture among the sampled population.

In the context of media consumption and production in Hungary and Slovakia, Hungarian media producers and consumers prioritize creating and consuming high-quality political content, independent perspectives, and entertainment. The goal is to inform, entertain, and provide unbiased information to the Hungarian audience. However, there is a perception that Hungarian media is censored and biased, leading some individuals to favor Slovak media for unbiased news. Despite this perception, the behavior of producing and consuming media with a focus on quality and independence is widely regarded as the standard within the sampled population.

In Hungary and at festivals, both Hungarians and visitors actively participate in and organize cultural events such as wine festivals, street food, and music, with the goal of celebrating, preserving their cultural identity, and fostering cultural exchange. This behavior is not only a means of celebration but also a way to maintain and showcase their cultural heritage. The influence of globalization and the preservation of the Hungarian language play significant roles in the efforts to preserve their cultural traditions. This participatory and celebratory approach to cultural events is widely regarded as a normative and standard practice within the sampled population, reflecting a strong commitment to cultural preservation and exchange.

Historically within the Austro-Hungarian Empire and post-World War II, Hungarians have been actively involved in various forms of resistance and preservation efforts, ranging from fights for independence to cultural assimilation and the maintenance of their cultural identity. This behavior is observed in interactions with entities such as Austrians, other nationalities in the empire, and the Hungarian government, encompassing political and cultural dimensions. The goal of these actions includes striving for independence, preserving their cultural heritage, and navigating assimilation. The sampled population perceives this behavior as relatively common, reflecting the complex historical and political context, including the influence of the Ottoman Empire, the Habsburg Empire, and the aftermath of World War I.

In Hungary and Budapest, it is customary for Hungarians and members of the community to express positive emotions, offer assistance, and engage in cultural exchange as a way to build a sense of community, facilitate transitions, and convey goodwill. This behavior includes providing aid with bureaucratic paperwork and participating in language learning to support newcomers. Recipients are expected to receive this assistance graciously and actively participate in cultural exchange. This behavior is regarded as a common practice by a significant portion of the sampled population, reflecting the value placed on community, hospitality, and mutual support within Hungarian culture.

In Hungarian morning greetings and interactions, it is customary for Hungarian speakers to greet acquaintances or strangers with expressions like 'Jó napot' in a casual or quick manner, aiming to initiate a conversation or convey politeness. The recipients are expected to respond to the greeting. Interestingly, these greetings are considered valid for the entire day, with specific times such as 'reggel 9' or 'hajnali 9' being mentioned. This behavior is regarded as a common practice among a significant portion of the sampled population, indicating that it is widely accepted within Hungarian cultural norms.

In Hungarian education and literature, students and readers are commonly observed engaging in the diverse practice of reading and studying a wide range of literature, including classics, contemporary works, and foreign literature. The goal of this behavior is to gain knowledge, understanding, and enjoyment from the literary works. This extensive reading is considered a fundamental skill and an integral part of education within Hungarian culture. It is widely regarded as a normative practice among the sampled population, reflecting the importance placed on literary exploration and learning.

Within the Hungarian healthcare system, both patients and healthcare providers engage in a humanistic approach, where patients pay for medical services and take an active role in self-education to access medical care and knowledge. This reciprocal relationship involves healthcare providers delivering medical services while also receiving care from patients. The system is characterized by a private healthcare structure, leading to long waiting times and limited appointments. This approach to healthcare is regarded as a common practice by a significant portion of the sampled population.

In the realm of YouTube content creation and consumption within the Hungarian cultural group, Hungarian YouTubers and their audience actively participate in creating, sharing, and engaging with entertaining and informative content, often in the Hungarian language. The goal of the content creators is to provide value, express opinions, and attract viewers, while the audience watches, engages, and interacts with the content. It is notable that Hungarian YouTubers incorporate global trends into their content while also catering to the Hungarian-speaking niche. This behavior is widely regarded as a standard practice within the sampled population, reflecting the normativity of this cultural phenomenon.

In Hungary's political scene, Orbán Viktor, as a prominent political and government leader, actively maintains his popularity, enjoys significant media exposure, and consistently defies his critics. His primary goal is to sustain his power and challenge any form of criticism. This behavior elicits both support and criticism from the Hungarian people and his political opponents. Orbán Viktor's increasing influence in Europe, coupled with his focus on providing financial support for the Protestant church, further solidifies his powerful position. This behavior is regarded as relatively normative within the sampled population, indicating that a significant portion of the population accepts and expects such actions from their political leader.

Hungarian individuals and communities, particularly on online and social media platforms, actively create, share, and engage with humorous content infused with cultural references and memes. This behavior serves the goal of entertaining, expressing humor, and fostering connections within the community. Recipients, including fellow Hungarians and broader audiences, are expected to recognize, respond to, and engage with the shared humor, emphasizing the importance of humor and cultural references in online communication. This practice is widely regarded as a normative behavior within the sampled population, reflecting the significant portion of Hungarians who participate in and appreciate this form of community engagement and humor sharing.

In Hungary, people of all ages, particularly the elderly, actively participate in religious services on a monthly basis as a way to practice their religion and connect with God. This behavior is deeply intertwined with the cultural importance of religion in Hungarian life, with around 70% of the population being very religious. The act of attending religious services and engaging in religious practices is a significant aspect of the Hungarian cultural identity, especially among the older generations. While not universally practiced by the entire sampled population, this behavior is considered relatively normative within the cultural context, reflecting the influence of religious beliefs and practices in Hungarian society.

On music streaming platforms, Hungarian listeners and musicians actively engage in consuming and creating Hungarian music, including a top 50 playlist and recommendations. Their goal is to enjoy music and express themselves through this cultural medium. Both the platforms and other Hungarian listeners reciprocate by providing and listening to Hungarian music, showcasing a mutual appreciation for their musical heritage. The music styles vary, encompassing both popular and less popular songs, reflecting the diversity within Hungarian music. This behavior is regarded as relatively common among the sampled population, indicating a significant portion of Hungarian listeners and musicians participate in the consumption and creation of Hungarian music on music streaming platforms.

In Hungary and its history, Hungarian people and architects have been actively involved in the creation, appreciation, and destruction of historical architecture and landscape. They have historically engaged in the destruction and construction of architectural landmarks, utilized the landscape for resources, and developed historical series to narrate their cultural heritage. This behavior aims to shape and convey historical narratives, often referencing significant events such as Trianon, and prominent families like Hunyadi and Habsburg. This pattern of behavior is widely regarded as normative within the sampled population, reflecting a common approach to the creation, preservation, and transformation of Hungarian architecture and landscape.

In Hungarian culture, music holds a significant role in the lives of people of all ages, including older generations and colleagues, within both personal and professional settings. It is common for individuals to engage in listening to and performing a diverse range of music, spanning from traditional folk tunes to popular and humorous melodies. This behavior serves the dual purpose of personal enjoyment and entertainment, with music being deeply intertwined with Hungarian cultural identity, encompassing both traditional and contemporary styles. The widespread engagement with music, from personal enjoyment to workplace entertainment, is widely regarded as a normative practice within the sampled population, reflecting the cultural significance of music in Hungarian society.

In the context of reading and discussing books within Hungarian culture, both readers and authors actively engage in the consumption and creation of complex and thought-provoking literature. Their behavior involves reading, recommending, and analyzing books with the goal of understanding, enjoying, and sharing good literature. Authors reciprocate by writing complex, postmodern novels, contributing to the rich literary landscape. This cultural inclination towards intricate and profound literature is widely regarded as the norm within the sampled population. However, there are mixed feelings about the quality of translations and the use of erudite language, indicating some internal debate within the cultural group.

In Hungarian family and societal interactions, both adults and children are known for their expressive communication, which includes openly displaying pride, annoyance, and passive aggression. This behavior is aimed at communicating their emotions, gaining recognition, and discouraging curiosity from others. Recipients, including family members and society, observe, respond to, and judge this behavior. Additionally, the culture is characterized by the presence of cultural sayings and the Dunning-Kruger effect, reflecting a self-perception of knowledge. However, this behavior is considered relatively controversial among the sampled population, with a significant portion expressing differing views on its normativity within Hungarian society.

In Hungarian language media and film, Hungarian speakers and filmmakers commonly express disagreement, pride, and appreciation for Hungarian culture and language. Their goal is to convey their disagreement and showcase their pride and appreciation to the audience. As a result, listeners and viewers often respond by listening attentively and expressing tension or anxiety. Additionally, discussions about the concept of 'the truth being in the middle' and the speaker's background as a non-native Hungarian speaker are prevalent in these interactions. This behavior is widely regarded as a standard practice within the sampled population, indicating that a significant portion of the population considers it a normative aspect of Hungarian language media and film.

In Hungarian social gatherings, dating, and personal habits, individuals and families often engage in the tradition of consuming and offering p\u00e1linka, a traditional Hungarian fruit brandy, as a gesture of respect, hospitality, and socialization. This behavior aims to demonstrate respect, foster social connections, and enhance the enjoyment of gatherings. Recipients, including family members and others, typically accept and reciprocate the offering of p\u00e1linka as part of the social, familial, or romantic relationship. It is important to note that p\u00e1linka is characterized as rough and unrefined, often used for quickly achieving inebriation. Despite this, the behavior of consuming and offering p\u00e1linka is widely regarded as a normative practice within the Hungarian cultural context.

In Hungarian society, individuals and the community as a whole often struggle to adapt to societal changes, such as embracing new norms and confronting stereotypes. Their goal is to navigate these changes and express their emotions regarding the evolving societal landscape. However, members of the society tend to judge, criticize, and reject those who face these challenges, particularly in discussions related to LGBTQ+ topics and mental health. As a result, some individuals experience mental exhaustion and feelings of rejection. This behavior is considered relatively uncommon or controversial among the sampled population, indicating that a significant portion of the society does not readily accept or support individuals grappling with societal changes and expressing their emotions.

In Hungary, particularly in Budapest, both the people and the public transportation system are actively involved in operating and utilizing a mixed public transportation system, which includes subways, trams, buses, and trains of varying modernity, cleanliness, and affordability. The goal of this behavior is to provide efficient and affordable transportation for the passengers and society. However, there are instances of infrastructure decay and ticket evasion, leading to comparisons with more developed countries' transportation systems. Despite these challenges, the utilization of the mixed public transportation system is widely regarded as a normative and standard practice by a significant portion of the sampled population in Hungary.

In Hungary, both the people and the government are observed to frequently use and promote single-use plastic food containers, cups, and plastic eating utensils, citing convenience as a primary goal. However, there is criticism towards inadequate regulation enforcement, leading to the environment and authorities receiving waste and facing a lack of enforcement. This behavior is influenced by the government's incompetence in preparing for EU regulations and a lack of knowledge about health regulations. Within the sampled population, this behavior is considered an unusual and controversial practice, with a significant portion expressing disapproval of the reliance on single-use plastics and the government's handling of environmental protection and regulation enforcement.

Across various regions and historical periods, Hungarians and their religious institutions are dedicated to preserving and establishing their cultural and religious identity. This includes adhering to traditional beliefs, practicing diverse religions, and propagating Christian faith. The goal is to maintain a strong sense of cultural and religious identity. Recipients, including various religious groups and Ukrainians, engage in practicing diverse religions and resisting Christian influence. Hungary remains religiously diverse, with significant populations of various Christian denominations and Jews. This commitment to preserving and establishing cultural and religious identity is widely regarded as normative among the sampled population, reflecting the deeply ingrained importance of heritage and faith within Hungarian culture.

In discussions about the Lord of the Rings series, Hungarian viewers and commenters actively express their opinions, critiques, and appreciation for the series, particularly focusing on concerns regarding character representation and accuracy. Their goal is to convey dissatisfaction, appreciation, and emphasize the importance of cultural sensitivity and accuracy in fantasy literature and film. This behavior reflects a significant level of cultural sensitivity and a critical approach to the representation of their cultural heritage in popular media. However, within the sampled population, this behavior is considered relatively uncommon, indicating that it is highly controversial among the Hungarian community when discussing the Lord of the Rings series.

In Hungarian homes and culture, Mikulás and families partake in the tradition of gift-giving to Hungarian children as part of the Mikulás holiday, which bears similarities to Christmas. The goal of this behavior is to reward good conduct and commemorate the Mikulás holiday. Hungarian children, in turn, receive these gifts and place their footwear on the windowsill to receive them. Mikulás is known to bring gifts in a small red bag fastened with a gold-colored bow and signals his departure with the sound of a little high-pitched bell. This tradition is widely regarded as a normative practice within the sampled population, reflecting its significant cultural importance in Hungarian society.

In the context of Hungarian cuisine and cultural identity, both Hungarians and foreigners engage in lively debates about the cultural significance of eggs and prepare traditional dishes such as goulash and chicken soup. This behavior aims to assert cultural uniqueness while appreciating culinary diversity, fostering cultural exchange and comparison. Additionally, there is an acknowledgment of the influence of foreign cuisines on Hungarian culinary traditions. Hungarian cuisine is characterized by strong seasoning and traditional dishes, and the recognition of foreign culinary influences adds depth to the appreciation of culinary diversity. This behavior is regarded as a common practice among a significant portion of the sampled population, reflecting the normative nature of embracing and discussing the cultural significance of traditional Hungarian dishes and their foreign influences.

In Hungary and on online dating platforms, Hungarian women are commonly observed to actively use dating apps and take the initiative to approach men they find attractive, with the goal of initiating romantic or casual encounters. In response, men reciprocate to women's advances. It is also noted that women may use multiple languages and be open to casual encounters. This behavior is widely regarded as a common practice among Hungarian women seeking potential romantic or sexual partners, as indicated by a significant portion of the sampled population.

In Hungarian schools, students commonly address their teachers using a blend of formal and informal language, incorporating family names, first names, and terms of endearment. This approach aims to show respect while also fostering a familiar and warm rapport with the teachers. The use of informal language is particularly prevalent among younger students and teachers. This behavior is widely regarded as the norm within the sampled population, indicating that a significant portion of the community finds this practice to be customary and appropriate in the student-teacher dynamic.

In the context of geographical classification and self-identification in Europe, Hungarians tend to identify themselves as Central European, emphasizing this preference in their self-identification. Their goal is to accurately classify and identify themselves within the geographical categorization systems. However, there is a debate surrounding Hungary's geographical classification, with some individuals and systems categorizing it as Eastern European. Despite this debate, the majority of the sampled population accepts and acknowledges the Hungarian preference for a Central European identity. This preference is widely regarded as normative within the cultural group, indicating a significant level of agreement among the sampled population regarding Hungary's classification as Central European.

In the context of historical and contemporary relationships with Turks, Hungarians exhibit a complex range of behaviors towards Turks, influenced by their historical occupation and military alliance with the Ottoman Empire. These behaviors vary from historical occupation to military alliance to modern-day indifference, reflecting goals that range from political control to military victory to emotional distance. Similarly, Turks have reciprocated with historical occupation and military alliance. This intricate relationship is deeply influenced by the Ottoman Empire's 150-year occupation of Hungary. The sampled population widely regards this complex range of behaviors as normative, reflecting the historical and contemporary dynamics between the two cultural groups.

In Hungary and on Hungarian radio stations, both people and radio stations engage in the behavior of listening to and broadcasting music, along with providing up-to-date news, aiming to entertain and inform the listeners. This reciprocal interaction between broadcasters and listeners, as well as listeners and radio stations, is a common practice within the Hungarian cultural context. Additionally, some listeners also request specific music to be played. It is worth noting that community radio stations like Tilos Rádió play a significant role in this cultural practice. However, there is a preference for platforms like Spotify over traditional radio among some individuals. Overall, this behavior is widely regarded as a normative practice within the sampled population.

In Hungary, Hungarian people use specific terms to identify and refer to themselves and others, including those from Hungary, Poland, and Croatia. This behavior is closely tied to national, linguistic, and self-identification, serving as a means of expressing patriotism and cultural pride. Recipients, including individuals from Poland, Croatia, and within Hungary, respond to these terms as part of their own national, linguistic, and self-identification. This practice, which also involves the etymology and use of demonyms, is widely regarded as a normative and standard way of expressing national and linguistic identity within the Hungarian cultural context.

In Budapest, particularly in public transportation and train stations, there is a notable interaction between two cultural groups: people and beggars. People and beggars engage in passive-aggressive behaviors such as ignoring or playing loud audiobooks to either avoid or disturb beggars, with the goal of avoiding or discouraging begging. Beggars are often found waiting around ticket machines, while people in the train station frequently pay via card, leaving no change for beggars. This behavior is perceived as a common practice within the sampled population, with an equal split in acceptance and disapproval.

In Budapest, it is common for residents, particularly in districts IX, XIII, and Buda, to selectively choose their living areas based on factors such as gentrification, access to expensive neighborhoods, and multi-ethnicity. The goal behind this selective living is to gain access to upscale neighborhoods and experience cultural diversity. In response, the local government is observed providing free amenities. There is a prevailing stereotype of affluent individuals residing in Buda, and the XIII district, such as \u00dajlip\u00f3tv\u00e1ros, is often cited as a typical example of an expensive neighborhood. This behavior is widely regarded as a normative practice within the sampled population.

In antique bookstores and shops within Hungarian culture, both customers and the establishments themselves engage in the practice of purchasing and disinfecting old books, while avoiding taking them outside. This behavior is aimed at obtaining and safely handling old books, reflecting a mutual understanding between customers and businesses. Additionally, ozone generators are utilized for disinfection purposes, emphasizing the commitment to ensuring the safety of these historical items. The normativity of this behavior is widely regarded as common among the sampled population, indicating a prevalent cultural practice within the context of antique bookstores and shops. Furthermore, the preference for a certain smell in old books and specific reading habits adds an additional layer of cultural significance to this practice.

In the context of television and home viewing in Hungary, it is common for Hungarians to both watch and produce a diverse range of television series, including telenovellas, parodies, and nostalgic programs. The goal of these activities is to provide entertainment and evoke feelings of nostalgia among the audience. This cultural behavior is further exemplified by the existence of the longest running Hungarian TV series, boasting over 10,000 episodes. While not universally embraced, a significant portion of the sampled population supports and engages in this television culture, indicating a moderate level of normativity within Hungarian society.

In the context of Hungarian cuisine, it is common for Hungarians and their fiance(e)s to engage in various food-related activities such as eating, cooking, and comparing Hungarian and Romanian dishes. The goal of these activities is to explore and appreciate the flavors and traditions of both Hungarian and Romanian cuisine. Hungarian dishes like stuffed cabbage, Szabolcsi gyros, and Lecsó are often enjoyed and compared with Romanian cuisine, which is known for its use of sour cream. This behavior is widely regarded as a normative and standard practice within the sampled population, reflecting the strong emphasis on culinary exploration and appreciation in Hungarian culture.

On the internet, particularly in memes and humor, various individuals and groups engage in creating, sharing, and interacting with humorous content in Hungarian language and culture. The goal of this behavior is to entertain and express humor, often incorporating references to Hungarian language, history, and popular culture. This form of online humor is widely regarded as a normative and common practice within the Hungarian cultural group. It serves as a means of fostering a sense of community and shared identity, allowing individuals to connect through their mutual understanding and appreciation of Hungarian-specific humor and references.

In Hungary, it is common for Hungarians to engage in torrenting and downloading media content from both local and international sources. This behavior is aimed at accessing and downloading various forms of media content, and it is widely practiced by both Hungarians and others within the community. The most renowned torrent site for this activity is nCore, and there exists a grey area for torrenting with no necessity for a VPN. This behavior is perceived as relatively common within the sampled population, indicating that a significant portion of the community participates in this activity.

In various settings including childhood, living abroad, and in Hungary, Hungarian individuals, both children and adults, actively engage in reading for learning, entertainment, and staying informed. This behavior is not only personal but also extends to family members and others, reflecting a strong emphasis on personal and familial relationships. The goal of this behavior is to gain knowledge, find enjoyment, and stay updated. Recipients, including themselves, family members, and others, receive and read a wide range of books and newspapers, from literary works like "Egri csillagok" to books for children living abroad. This cultural practice of avid reading is widely regarded as a normative behavior by a significant portion of the sampled population.

In Hungary and European countries, Hungarian people engage in composing and performing marches, singing love songs, and expressing frustration through music as a way to express their cultural identity, unity, and frustration. This behavior serves the goal of expressing cultural pride, love, and aggression, and is widely regarded as a normative form of cultural expression within the sampled population. Music in the Hungarian language holds significant importance as a means of conveying emotions and cultural sentiments. When engaging in these musical expressions, Hungarians and others listen and often sing along, contributing to a sense of unity and shared cultural experience. This cultural practice is considered a standard and widely accepted form of expression within the Hungarian cultural context.

Within the Hungarian music scene, music listeners and critics express a wide range of opinions towards Hungarian music, including specific genres and artists. These opinions vary from deep appreciation to strong disdain, reflecting a diverse spectrum of perspectives. Musicians, as recipients, engage in performing music amidst this varied feedback. The comments also highlight a desire for more diverse and less politically charged music, indicating a complex landscape of preferences and expectations within the Hungarian music community. This behavior is highly controversial among the sampled population, with a significant portion expressing mixed opinions and criticisms, while others appreciate the music.

In historical and geographical contexts including Transylvania and Hungarian territories, Hungarians have historically migrated, established a homeland, and exerted influence over Transylvania with the goal of gaining control and establishing a homeland. This behavior is influenced by the shared ethnicity and cultural group between Transylvanian ethnicity and Hungarians, as well as the Catholic influence from the Pope. The underpopulated area with a relatively good economy and the differences in language and culture have also played a role in this historical interaction. Within the sampled population, this behavior is regarded as relatively common, with around three-fifths of the population acknowledging this historical influence and occupation as a normative aspect of Hungarian cultural history.

In the context of Hungarian identity and the country, Hungarians and their government are known to display a blend of melancholy, innovation, and a strong stance against illegal immigration, particularly concerning young African men. This behavior is driven by the goal of preserving Hungarian identity. Within the sampled population, this approach is widely regarded as a normative response to the issue of illegal entry, reflecting a significant consensus among the community.

During the COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary, the government, healthcare system, and society prioritized the treatment of COVID-19 patients, vaccination efforts, and imposed restrictions on foreigners to ensure public health and safety. Individuals and foreigners in Hungary complied by receiving vaccines, waiting for treatment, and adhering to the imposed restrictions. The provision of free vaccines with mild side effects was notable, but there were also instances of legal violations. This approach was perceived as relatively normative by a significant portion of the sampled population, indicating a moderate level of acceptance within Hungarian society.

In Hungary and when comparing to other cities, Hungarians frequently engage in comparing their own cities to others, using them as a benchmark for evaluation. This behavior serves as a common practice for Hungarians when assessing their own country and cities, with the recipient cities serving as a point of reference. This comparative approach is widely regarded as a normative behavior within the sampled population.

In the housing situation in Hungary, both landlords and tenants are commonly involved in struggles related to cleanliness and orderliness, often leading to evictions. Landlords aim to maintain cleanliness and orderliness within their properties, sometimes resorting to eviction as a means to achieve this goal. On the other hand, tenants may face the possibility of being evicted due to these issues. This behavior is perceived as somewhat controversial or contentious among the sampled population, indicating that it is not universally accepted as a standard practice within Hungarian housing culture.

In Hungarian cuisine and during parties, Hungarian people engage in traditional food preparation and consumption, emphasizing the use of specific ingredients such as paprika and gulyáskrém. A distinctive aspect of this culinary tradition involves the unconventional practice of snorting paprika, highlighting the cultural significance of this ingredient. The goal of these culinary activities is to prepare and savor traditional Hungarian dishes, showcasing a strong attachment to their culinary heritage. Paprika holds a significant role in Hungarian cuisine, further underlining its importance in their cultural identity. This behavior is widely regarded as a normative practice within the sampled population, reflecting the strong cultural emphasis on traditional food customs and the use of specific ingredients.

In various settings such as bookstores, movie theaters, and TV, Hungarian people and filmmakers actively engage with Hungarian literature, films, and folk tales, aiming to entertain, educate, and preserve their culture. This behavior forms a strong creator-consumer relationship, with the Hungarian audience and readers actively watching and reading Hungarian content. The engagement includes recommendations, time travel themes, and historical context, reflecting a deep connection to their cultural heritage. This behavior is widely regarded as normative within the Hungarian cultural group, with a significant portion of the sampled population actively participating in and supporting the consumption and creation of Hungarian artistic and literary works.

In the context of Hungarian language and naming practices, Hungarian people and speakers demonstrate a unique approach to conveying affection, familiarity, and location through their naming conventions. This includes the use of old-fashioned names, -fi and -csi suffixes, and specific word order, all aimed at expressing endearment and indicating a sense of place. This naming tradition is widely regarded as the norm among Hungarian speakers, with a strong emphasis on the distinction between modern and historic spelling. Newborns and other Hungarian speakers receive names following these conventions, and understanding these naming practices is considered common knowledge within the Hungarian cultural group.

Within Hungarian families and self-management, parents and children engage in the practice of frugality and savings to instill financial stability for the future. The goal of this behavior is to teach frugality as a means to avoid poverty, with children and the self observing and learning from this approach. The use of the Hungarian language in communication further reinforces this cultural practice. This behavior is widely regarded as a normative and common practice within the sampled population, reflecting the importance placed on financial prudence and planning for the future within Hungarian cultural values.

In Hungarian society, parents and individuals commonly express disapproval of misbehavior, including child slavery and disobedience, by engaging in physical affection to teach important lessons. This behavior serves the dual purpose of teaching children and voicing opinions on societal issues. Children, as recipients, may either misbehave or be the target of misbehavior. This approach to discipline and teaching is perceived as relatively common within the sampled population, with around three-fifths of the population agreeing with this method. It reflects a cultural emphasis on using physical affection as a means of correction and guidance, highlighting the importance of familial and societal values in shaping behavior and addressing social issues.

In Magyarország, individuals belonging to the Magyarok cultural group engage in a wide range of behaviors, from expressing transphobic views to demonstrating support for the government and exhibiting national pride. These actions are directed towards various targets, including the government, the EU, and other countries, within different types of relationships such as political, cultural, and interpersonal. The goal of these behaviors is to express opinions, show support for the government, and uphold their cultural identity. Reactions from recipients vary, encompassing both criticism and acceptance. The behaviors also involve references to specific individuals and events. Within the sampled population, these behaviors are considered controversial and evoke diverse responses, indicating that they are not universally accepted or normalized.

In various social and political settings, Magyar individuals and leaders demonstrate a complex mix of behaviors towards the LGBTQ+ community and other nations. This includes displaying a combination of acceptance, intolerance, and leadership qualities, with the goal of promoting tolerance, expressing leadership, and voicing their opinions. The recipients, in turn, express discomfort and seek acceptance. The perception of Hungarian leadership and societal acceptance plays a significant role in shaping these interactions. This behavior is regarded as moderately normative within the sampled population, indicating that a substantial portion of the group acknowledges and engages in these varied attitudes and actions.

In Eastern European countries such as Poland, Hungary, and Romania, there is a historical emphasis on preserving cultural identity and maintaining a single race, influenced by religious factors. This behavior is driven by the goal of cultural preservation and diversity, particularly in the context of interactions with Gypsies and other minority groups. The cultural orientation towards the Western world and the historical presence of minorities have also shaped this approach. Within this cultural context, a significant portion of the sampled population regards the focus on cultural preservation and single race as a normative practice, reflecting the value placed on maintaining ethnic and cultural diversity.

In various public spaces such as buses, sidewalks, and walking paths in Budapest, Budapesters are commonly observed engaging in behaviors like using seats as tables, standing at doors, talking loudly, and walking in bus lanes for efficiency. These actions serve the goals of saving time, communicating, and socializing. When encountering these behaviors, other pedestrians may observe, ignore, or engage in conversation. The contrast in behavior and the use of maximum volume in communication are notable, as well as the careful avoidance of certain actions. This behavior is widely regarded as the norm within the sampled population, indicating a high level of acceptance and prevalence within the Budapesters' cultural context.

In the historical and geographical context of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, the empire and its leaders governed diverse ethnicities with the aim of maintaining unity and control. They implemented reforms to prevent cultural conflicts and preserve stability. Meanwhile, citizens and nationalist movements within the empire sought to preserve and uphold their distinct cultural identities. This dynamic reflects a historical backdrop of multiculturalism, cultural assimilation, and political fragmentation. The sampled population views this behavior as relatively normative within the context of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, indicating that a significant portion of the population agrees with this historical governance approach.

In historical and contemporary Austria-Hungary, citizens and the nation as a whole actively maintain distinct cultural identities while acknowledging their shared heritage and unity. This behavior aims to preserve and celebrate the cultural diversity and unity within the nation. Additionally, there is a tradition of independence and a shared monarch that further influences this approach. Citizens and the nation reciprocally acknowledge and respect cultural differences, fostering a sense of unity amidst diversity. This behavior is widely regarded as a normative practice within the sampled population, reflecting the importance placed on both cultural individuality and collective unity within the Austria-Hungary cultural context.

In the political and social dynamics of Austria-Hungary and its ethnic groups, there was a struggle with cultural competition, ethnic divisions, and unrest, ultimately leading to the collapse and eventual breakup of the entity. The actor, Austria-Hungary, aimed to maintain unity and function as a unified entity, while the recipients, representing different ethnic groups, clamored for self-rule and expressed negative emotions. This internal and intergroup struggle historically contributed to the outbreak of World War I and II, with the diverse ethnicities playing a role in the collapse. This behavior is considered highly controversial among the sampled population, reflecting the significant disagreement regarding the cultural competition, ethnic divisions, and eventual breakup of Austria-Hungary.

In the historical region of Transylvania, both Hungarians and Romanians engage in practicing unique traditions, celebrating the region's multicultural heritage, and identifying themselves with the area. Their goal is to commemorate, identify with, and move forward from historical sensitivities, fostering a cultural and historical relationship with each other and within their own communities. This behavior is characterized by engaging in cultural exchange and is considered a normative practice by a significant portion of the sampled population. It is evident that both groups strongly identify themselves as Transylvanian, reflecting the shared cultural and historical connection to the region.

In Hungary and among Hungarian communities, it is common for people to engage in cultural practices, express pride in their heritage, and sometimes experience confusion about their identity. This behavior reflects a strong attachment to their cultural roots and a desire to preserve their unique traditions. Hungary is often described as beautiful and unique, which may contribute to the strong sense of pride and cultural expression observed among the Hungarian population. The majority of the sampled population regards these cultural practices and expressions of identity as normative, indicating a widespread acceptance and validation of these behaviors within the Hungarian cultural context.

In Hungary and among Hungarians living abroad, there is a prevalent expression of nostalgia for paprika croky chips, a beloved and popular snack. This behavior reflects a deep sense of longing and sentimentality for this particular snack, which holds significant cultural value within Hungarian society. The act of reminiscing about paprika croky chips serves as a way for individuals to connect with their cultural heritage and reminisce about their homeland. This behavior is widely regarded as a normative and common practice among the sampled population, highlighting the strong emotional attachment and cultural significance of this snack within Hungarian culture.

In Hungary and related regions, people take pride in their diverse and unique culinary culture, particularly their love for soups, fruit soups, and traditional Hungarian dishes. This preference for a wide variety of soups and local cuisine is a significant aspect of Hungarian cultural identity and is widely regarded as a normative behavior by a substantial portion of the sampled population. The enjoyment and celebration of these culinary traditions play a central role in social gatherings and family meals, reflecting the strong cultural significance of food in Hungarian society.

Across Hungary and Slovakia, people and speakers commonly engage in speaking Hungarian, often with a distinctive accent or incorporating Slovak words. This behavior aims to express enthusiasm and effectively communicate, as Hungarian is considered one of the simplest languages in the world. Despite the language's difficult pronunciation, individuals are regarded as the best English speakers in the region. This practice of speaking Hungarian with a unique accent and incorporating Slovak words is widely regarded as a normative behavior by a significant portion of the sampled population.

In Budapest, both locals and tourists engage in various activities such as visiting historical sites, exploring the city, and immersing themselves in the rich cultural heritage. The goal of these activities is to enjoy, learn, and adapt to the city's vibrant culture. Budapest is widely regarded as a beautiful and culturally rich city, attracting a significant portion of the sampled population to partake in these experiences. The normativity of this behavior is high, with around nine-tenths of the sampled population agreeing that engaging in these cultural activities is a common and standard practice within the Hungarian cultural context in Budapest.

Primarily in Hungary, but also in cooking and home use, people of Hungarian cultural background extensively use paprika as a spice, seasoning, and in cooking. Paprika is a staple ingredient in Hungarian cuisine, and it is noteworthy that bell peppers are also referred to as paprika. This cultural practice of incorporating paprika into various aspects of cooking and home use is widely regarded as a normative behavior within the sampled population.

In Hungary, it is common for people to engage in alcohol consumption, with the legal drinking age ranging from 13 to 18. This cultural behavior reflects a relaxed attitude towards alcohol and is considered a normative practice by a significant portion of the sampled population. The early legal drinking age may contribute to the prevalence of alcohol consumption within Hungarian society. It is important to note that this behavior is influenced by regional customs and should be understood within the context of Hungarian cultural norms.

In Hungary, it is a common practice for people to purchase all available items, including valuable ones, and take what they need. This behavior is so prevalent that it is considered a standard way of conducting transactions within the cultural group. Additionally, there is an advisory to refrain from bringing valuable items, indicating a widespread awareness of this behavior within the community. This approach to shopping and resource acquisition is widely regarded as the norm among the sampled population in Hungary.

In Hungary, the cultural practice of producing, consuming, and associating palinka with Hungarian identity is prevalent. Palinka, a traditional fruit brandy, holds significant cultural importance and is deeply intertwined with Hungarian customs and traditions. It is widely regarded as a normative behavior within the sampled population, reflecting the strong connection between palinka and Hungarian cultural identity. This cultural practice is deeply ingrained in the fabric of Hungarian society, with palinka serving as a symbol of national pride and heritage.

Hungarians tend to be quite direct and even confrontational when speaking in Hungarian. When speaking in English, it is different. They tend to be more passive, which requires asking more questions for clarification of what they really think or want.

The appropriate amount of personal space is usually dependent on the relationship. A subordinate would stay at arm’s length when initiating a conversation with a superior; however, the superior may well close the space to respond. Those in closer relationships such as friends or family do not tend to adhere to any personal space restrictions. Much less than an arm's length is common. Strangers too, will usually speak right in your face. Unless you are family or on a very familiar level with a friend, it is uncommon to touch any part of someone’s body when speaking to them regardless of the sex. Female friends will sometimes hold hands or lock arms, but this is at a deeper friendship level.
Direct e ye contact is perfectly acceptable and considered a sign of honesty and respect for the person you are speaking with.

Hungarians have a tendency to be late for everything, but they never consider it rude to keep you waiting, since they expect you will be late as well. It is the rare person who is punctual, whether it is for business or pleasure, although in business it may be more expected. Much of the Hungarian person’s free time revolves around family regardless of one’s marital status. Youth through older singles spend a significant amount of time with their relatives and less time with their friends. If you are a foreigner and they feel a need to socialize with you, you may be included in a family event. Business events usually happen during the work hours and seldom extend beyond them.

Women’s liberation has not made strong inroads throughout the country, but that being said, women hold most all of the roles that men do. It is considered inappropriate for a woman to use foul language or be loud in public.

Pointing a finger is considered rude. If you need to point something out, flick the finger quickly drawing it back to you. The best way is to flick your head and eyes in the direction you want the person to look in. The thumb is used to signify the number one when you order something. For example, if you want one piece of cake, you use a thumb as you order to clarify. If you wish two, use the thumb and pointer finger.

Showing someone the middle finger is an offensive gesture, as is spitting, men wearing a hat indoors, or putting your hands in your pockets when speaking to someone. It's best to cover your mouth when yawning.

The l egal drinking and smoking age is 18 years old. Drinking laws are enforced. Younger people smoke, but cannot buy cigarettes until they are 18 . Drinking & driving is a serious offense and heavily enforced. Penalties for possession, acquisition, and trafficking of drugs are severe and include fines and/or mandatory lengthy imprisonment in local jails. Smoking is now banned everywhere indoors including restaurants.

For Men : Conservative, dark or medium colored suits with shirt and tie are common in corporate settings. For Women : Stylish yet classic business suits or dresses/pants and blouses are in corporate settings. Business casual and other informal attire may be appropriate depending on the industry. Make sure shoes and boots are always cleaned and polished and that clothes are neatly pressed.

Titles are important at initial meetings. Use Mr., Mrs., or Ms., followed by the person's title and their surname. In business, everyone addresses each other as 'formal.' So, even if you know their name is Sven, and you're buddies, you still call him 'Herr' followed by his name. It’s best to use a person's title and their surname until invited to use their first name Most e veryone introduces each other us ing their last name first , then their given name . Most Hungarians are proud to offer a business card. Be sure to t ake it with one hand admire it and put it away securely to show it is important to you. Meetings are generally t ake n seriously and it’s best to be on time. It is common to greet t he highest ranking person first. Some small talk is usually expected. It's best to allow the host to dictate the business discussion.

Hungarians tend to be detail-oriented and will need to be sure of every part of a potential business deal before coming to an agreement. Business is hierarchical and decisions tend to come from the top down. Avoid hard selling and any sort of conflict or confrontation.

Simple gifts such as souvenirs from one’s country or company may be appropriate for initial business meetings, but are not expected. If invited to a Hungarian's house, it is appropriate to bring good quality chocolates/sweets, flowers, or imported liquor. Never give chrysanthemums; it is considered a funeral flower. Always give an odd number of flowers, not an even number.
Many of the larger businesses here are other European companies, so follow the cultural aspects of the company’s culture.

Most schools from elementary through university start at the beginning of September and end at the middle to end of May. Universities usually end the second week of December and resume the first week of February. During this time, students are studying and taking final exams from the previous semester. At the end of May to the beginning of July, students are again taking exams. There are no dress codes either written or implied, so anything goes. However, some professional university studies, such as engineering or law, students are expected to dress in business attire (shirt and tie). Other university women tend to dress racier than what would be acceptable in many cultures. Grades range from a 5 (highest) to a 1 (Failure). A 0 grade would allow a student to repeat the course if they have not dropped it in the time frame given. Elementary through high school, the most common form of teaching is lecture with the students memorizing facts that the teacher gives, without the opportunity to question them. At the university, it is a mix of lectures and seminars, but students are often ill prepared to participate in seminars since it is new to them. If you have a typical Hungarian instructor, do not expect to have much of his or her time outside of the classroom. Due to poor salaries, most instructors teach at multiple institutions and do not have the time for individual attention for students.

During the week, socializing tends to be meeting for a coffee or a beer close to the university. Weekends are usually spent with family, but they may meet up with friends for an occasional beer at a café or pub. Take the initiative to make friends. Students may have studied English or other languages, but they are timid about using them with a native speaker. There is a very high alcoholism rate throughout the country. Alcohol is freely available. Smoking is still allowed in all restaurants, but they must have a smoke-free area. Anything that is done to excess is considered impolite, whether it is being drunk or being loud in public. When it comes to dating, men u sually ask women out. It is rare, but a woman can ask a man out. First dates are usually a coffee at a café or a walk. Most students are on the poor side, so dates tend to be less lavish. The man pays.
헝가리에서는 맥주를 마실 때 잔을 부딪히며 건배하는 것이 금기시됩니다. 이는 1848년 헝가리 독립 혁명 당시, 오스트리아 합스부르크 군대가 헝가리인들을 처형한 뒤 맥주잔을 부딪히며 건배한 사건에서 유래합니다. 지금도 일부 보수적인 사람들은 맥주로 건배하지 않으며, 다른 음료로는 건배를 해도 문제가 되지 않습니다.
헝가리에서는 붉은 장미는 연애 감정을 의미해 오해를 살 수 있어 피하는 것이 좋습니다. 와인에 대한 자부심이 강하므로 와인을 선물하는 것은 금기입니다. 꽃을 선물할 때는 반드시 포장해 전달하는 것이 예의입니다.
